data.narrative:
Anatar is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company led by founder Kaia Rhodes. The peer universe consists of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), with particular relevance assigned to three same-stage, same-sector private peers: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

The peer-median method is the applicable valuation approach given data availability. The median valuation across the three Series C robotics peers is $1.0B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. This method anchors the central estimate given the direct comparability of stage and sector. The broader peer set—including Divergent and Exotec—provides contextual validation of the robotics and manufacturing subsector, though these were not included in the primary triangulation due to stage or operational divergence.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $850M (low) to $1.1B (high), centered on $1.0B. Key uncertainties include Anatar's specific operational metrics relative to the peer set—revenue growth rate, unit economics, and technology differentiation—which are not reflected in this stage-and-sector-only comparison. The single applicable method limits confidence; additional data on comparable transaction multiples or Anatar's financial performance would refine this estimate. The peer range of $1.0B to $1.6B reflects meaningful dispersion that warrants further investigation into performance drivers across the cohort.
